title: Projective normalization and unit locus of a radical curve extension
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $C$ a smooth projective integral $K$-curve, with $F=K(C)$. Let $U\subseteq C$ be an open subscheme, $n\geq1$ an integer invertible in $K$, and $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in F^	imes$ a finite list such that each $a_j$ and $a_j^{-1}$ is regular on $U$. Choose $\alpha_j$ in an algebraic closure of $F$ with $\alpha_j^n=a_j$, and put $L=F(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)$. Assume $L/F$ is finite. Let $
u:Y	o C$ be the normalization of $C$ in $L$. Then $Y$ is a normal integral projective $K$-curve, $
u$ is finite and surjective, and $
u^{-1}(U)	o U$ is etale. The canonical generic morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L	o Y$ identifies $K(Y)$ with the specified extension $L/F$, compatibly with the morphism to $C$. Here normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. No geometric integrality of $C$ and no roots of unity in $K$ are assumed. The cases $r=0$, $n=1$, and $U=\varnothing$ are included.

Notions: [def-weil-field], [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-pc-curve].

proof.text: The curve $C$ is Noetherian, by finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$. It is regular, with regular local rings, by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], so $C$ is normal by [rem-pc-regular-normal](1). On every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq C$, [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies $A$ with a domain in $F$ and $F$ with its fraction field. The affine stalk identifications give normality of every $A_{\mathfrak p}$; [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] therefore makes $A$ an integrally closed domain. These assertions hold without geometric integrality or perfection of $K$.

source.place: Tag 0569, lemma-regular-normal; algebra.tex Tag 030B, lemma-normality-is-local; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian. Regularity over an arbitrary field: varieties.tex Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular.

proof.text: By [def-fin-normalization-extension], $\nu^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A_L$, where $A_L$ is the integral closure of $A$ in the specified field $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $A_L$ is a normal domain with fraction field $L$. Its prime localizations are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], so every stalk of $Y$ is a normal domain. These affine charts are nonempty and reduced. The canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$ belongs to every such chart and is its generic point, because $\operatorname{Frac}A_L=L$. Hence its image is dense in every chart and therefore in $Y$. Thus $Y$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, so integral. Moreover [lem-sbc-normalization-generic-field] identifies this very generic morphism with $\operatorname{Spec}K(Y)\to Y$. Its composite to $C$ is the original map induced by $F\hookrightarrow L$, giving the required compatibility of function fields.

source.place: Tag 034L, lemma-integral-closure-in-normal; Tag 00GY, lemma-localize-normal-domain; morphisms.tex Tag 035P, lemma-description-normalization. Generic-field compatibility also follows from the cited project declaration.

proof.text: Since $C$ is integral of finite type over $K$ and $L/F$ is finite, [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite] gives finiteness of $\nu$. On the affine charts of step 2, $A\hookrightarrow A_L$ is injective and integral. By [pqf-lem-lying-over], every prime of $A$ lifts to a prime of $A_L$. These charts cover $C$, so $\nu$ is surjective.

source.place: Tags 035B, lemma-ubiquity-nagata, and 0AVK, lemma-nagata-normalization-finite-general, applied to the finite generic field extension; algebra.tex Tag 00GU, lemma-integral-going-up, and Tag 00GQ, lemma-integral-overring-surjective.

proof.text: For every affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ used above, the injective integral map $A\hookrightarrow A_L$ satisfies $\dim A_L=\dim A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal]. Apply [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] to the covering of $C$ by these $V$ and the covering of $Y$ by their inverse images. The two suprema coincide; thus $\dim Y=\dim C=1$.

source.place: Tag 00OK, lemma-integral-sub-dim-equal; properties.tex Tag 04MU, lemma-dimension; schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves; algebra.tex Tag 00KG, lemma-dimension-height.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $T=C$ and $h=\nu$. The base is affine and Noetherian, the structure map of $C$ has the stipulated finite projective-space embedding, and $\nu$ is finite by step 3. Its affine-base conclusion gives a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_K$ for some finite $N$. Thus $Y$ is projective in exactly the convention of [def-kun-projective]; [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes its structure map proper, hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Together with steps 2 and 4 (integral, dimension exactly $1$) it is a curve over $K$ in the sense of [def-pc-curve], hence a normal integral projective $K$-curve.

source.place: Tag 0B3I, lemma-finite-projective, and Tag 01WE, lemma-H-projective-composition; the cited node supplies the finite projective-space conclusion over an affine Noetherian base.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$. All $a_j$ lie in $A^\times$, and $n$ is a unit in $A$. Put $B_0=A$ and recursively $B_j=B_{j-1}[T_j]/(T_j^n-a_j)$. At each stage the images of $n$ and $a_j$ remain units, so [lem-sfb-unit-binomial-finite-etale] makes $\operatorname{Spec}B_j\to\operatorname{Spec}B_{j-1}$ finite etale, with a free module basis of length $n$. Inductively composing these morphisms, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2) show that $\operatorname{Spec}B_r\to V$ is finite etale. For $r=0$ this is the identity of $V$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence, explicit unit-root algebra in the proof; morphisms.tex Tags 01WK, lemma-composition-finite, and 02GN, lemma-composition-etale.

proof.text: The chosen roots define an $F$-algebra homomorphism $B_r\otimes_A F\to L$ sending $T_j$ to $\alpha_j$. Its image is $F[\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r]$. The iterated monic bases from step 6 show that this image is finite-dimensional over $F$; it is a domain because it lies in $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] it is a field, hence equals $F(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)=L$. Thus the map is surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-normal-generic-components] to $\operatorname{Spec}B_r\to V$: the base $V$ is normal integral and Noetherian by step 1. The generic algebra is the finite product of the component fields stated there. A homomorphism from this finite product onto the field $L$ selects exactly one factor (its orthogonal idempotents map to $0$ or $1$ with exactly one mapping to $1$), and that factor maps isomorphically to $L$. The same cited node says its normalization over $V$ is finite etale. This normalization is $\operatorname{Spec}A_L=\nu^{-1}(V)$, with the specified $A$-map, by [def-fin-normalization-extension].

source.place: Tag 0BQL, lemma-finite-etale-covering-normal-unramified, including its component argument; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field.

proof.text:
For each affine $V\subseteq U$ from step 6, step 7 gives $
u^{-1}(V)	o V$ etale. The inclusion $V\hookrightarrow U$ is etale and its composite with that map is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2). The opens $
u^{-1}(V)$ cover $
u^{-1}(U)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] gives $
u^{-1}(U)	o U$ etale. If $U=\varnothing$, the same criterion with the empty covering gives the assertion. When $r=0$, the generic map in step 7 is $F	o F$; when $n=1$, every root algebra is its base ring. All preceding steps apply to these cases. No argument adjoins roots of unity or changes the constant field.
